newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hokkaido Bank says planned merger could be delayed.
newsitem.headline: Hokkaido Bank says planned merger could be delayed.

text.p: Regional Japanese bank Hokkaido Bank Ltd said on Tuesday that a merger with city bank Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd planned for April 1, 1998, could be delayed if the two banks cannot come up with business rationalisation plans by the end of September.

A Hokkaido Bank spokesman quoted bank president Tsuneo Fujita as telling a news conference on Monday that it was not an easy task for the two banks to come up with rationalisation plans, and that the merger could be delayed from the planned date of April 1, depending on ongoing discussions of the plans.

The spokesman told Reuters that one of the most difficult tasks for the two banks in drafting the plans was on how to establish a common standard in assessing their bad loan holdings and reach a consensus on how the two should tackle bad loan problems.

In April, Hokkaido Takushoku, Japan's 10th-largest commercial bank, said it would merge with the smaller Hokkaido Bank and cease its overseas operations in order to become a "super-regional" bank. The two said they would merge as equals by April 1998.

The Hokkaido Bank spokesman said that the two banks were due to make public their rationalisation plans in September, adding that the process was necessary to gain understanding from shareholders and business clients of the new bank.
Some analysts recently said that the planned merger could still be called off.

Hokkaido Takushoku, which forecast 3.0 billion yen in parent current profits in 1997/98, may be forced to post losses if Tokyo stock prices fall. If that happens, the planned merger might run into trouble, they said.
